howToApply: Resolve every `over.selector` to a TEXT node id (history-resolve-ids.mjs understands the same selector shape) and every `to.newBoardName` to the id add-state-board.mjs printed, then run: node scripts/figma/add-hotspots.mjs <this file> --apply. add-hotspots.mjs expects rows {over,to,name,pad,why} with plain ids — flatten before running.
convention: 'hotspot/state · X' is this file's convention for a prototype jump to a sibling state (386 instances measured section-wide, per COVER-2-11); 'hotspot/back · X' is a real back path. These are all forward jumps.

selector.hint: the clickable timestamp in a change row; ActivityView.tsx:600-612 renders it as .entry-time inside .entry-meta

rows.name: hotspot/state · changes-restore-confirm
rows.why: UX-I-01 — the timestamp is the control that produces the confirm. A board-level reaction would make the whole change list clickable, which is the defect add-hotspots.mjs exists to avoid (wire-edges.mjs walks a TEXT node up to its nearest frame ancestor, and here that IS the board).

selector.hint: the header action; ActivityView.tsx:491-500 renders 'Clear' beside the 'Undo History' label. If AMBIG against 'Clear all', take the one whose characters are exactly 'Clear'.
the preview label; TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:343. It is the node that lies when there is no frame, so it is the door onto the no-preview board.
the list header; ActivityView.tsx:467. The boundary is the END of this list, so the door onto it is the header, not a control.
the empty-state title; ActivityView.tsx:766. Only present on a board drawn in the empty state — if NOMATCH on 163:2, retarget to 163:64 History · Saves · empty.

rows.name: hotspot/state · changes-load-error
rows.why: UX-I-06 — the two states this pairs are the pair the finding is about: 'nothing happened' vs 'I could not read it'. Putting the edge between them is what makes the difference visible in the prototype.

selector.hint: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:471-482 '+ Save a version' at the foot of the panel

rows.name: hotspot/state · saves-overflow
rows.why: UX-I-08 — the overflow belongs beside the one control that already writes to the version store.

selector.hint: a disabled-undo affordance if the board draws one; expect NOMATCH — recorded so the applier knows the door for undo-unavailable was looked for and not found, and must be placed by hand or the board left as a terminal state.
